'''Kentavious Tannell Caldwell-Pope''' (born February 18, 1993) is an American college basketball player. He plays guard, and was one of the top high school basketball players in the class of 2011.<ref>[http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Kentavious-Caldwell-Pope-77197 Rivals Player Profile], rivals.yahoo.com. Retrieved 10 March 2011.</ref> Caldwell-Pope played [[college basketball]] for [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] for two years beofore declaring for the [[2013 NBA Draft]] on April 15, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2013/04/15/georgia-sophomore-star-entering-nba-draft/2084371/|title=Georgia sophomore star entering NBA draft|date=April 15, 2013|publisher=USA Today |accessdate=April 15, 2013}}</ref>

==High school==
Caldwell-Pope was a highly heralded player in high school. As a senior, he averaged 31 points and 8.2 rebounds per game at [[Greenville High School (Greenville, Georgia)|Greenville High School]] in [[Greenville, Georgia]].  He led the Patriots to the State Class A Final Four in 2011 and to consecutive Sweet 16 berths in 2009-10.  

He was named to several prominent high school All-America teams as a senior, including being selected to play in the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2011 McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref name=MCD>{{cite web| last = White | first = Chris | title =http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2011/02/10/1454929/high-school-basksetball-greenvilles.html | publisher = Ledger-Enquirer | date = February 10, 2011 | url =http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2011/02/10/1454929/high-school-basksetball-greenvilles.html | accessdate = March 16, 2013}}</ref> and the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].<ref>[http://www.jordanbrandclassic.com/Teams/2011-jordan-brand-classic-west-team.html 2011 Jordan Brand Classic: West Team], jordanbrandclassic.com. Retrieved 15 March 2011.</ref>  

As a senior, he was rated the nation's No. 3 shooting guard prospect, the No. 12 prospect overall, by recruiting analysts for Rivals.com.

==College career==
Caldwell-Pope chose Georgia over scholarship offers from Alabama, Florida State, Georgia Tech, and Tennessee among others.

===Freshman season===
As a freshman, Caldwell-Pope was named to the Coaches' Freshman All-SEC Team, which also included NBA lottery picks [[Bradley Beal]], [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]], and [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]].  His highest output as a freshman was 25 points vs. Ole Miss, which was the most by a UGA freshman in almost 13 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320210061|title= Mississippi 66, Georgia 63|date=January 21, 2012|publisher=ESPN |accessdate=January 21, 2012}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
As a sophomore, Caldwell-Pope was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] after averaging 18.5 points and 7.1 rebounds per game.<ref name=POY>{{cite web| last = Lockridge & Cole| first = | title =Georgia's Kentavious Caldwell-Pope named SEC's top player | publisher = The Tennessean | date = March 12, 2013 | url =http://www.tennessean.com/article/20130312/SPORTS06/303120093/Georgia-s-Kentavious-Caldwell-Pope-named-SEC-s-top-player | accessdate = March 16, 2013}}</ref> He ended his career at Georgia scoring a career-high 32 points and 13 rebounds in a loss against LSU at the SEC tournament in Nashville.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330730061|title=LSU 68, Georgia 63|date=March 14, 2013|publisher=ESPN |accessdate=March 14, 2013}}</ref>
